chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
He does not shave his head nor visit (the Prophet's shrine) until he offers the sacrifice (qurbani), then he shaves his head and visits whenever he wishes.

key_terms.يَزُورُ: to visit (specifically the shrine of the Prophet or Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the required order of shaving the head and visiting the shrine in relation to the sacrifice during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural sequence of Hajj rituals, emphasizing that the sacrificial offering (dhabh) is the prerequisite condition for both shaving the head (halq) and performing the shrine visit (ziyarat). It highlights the scholarly view that while the core ritual completion depends on the sacrifice, the subsequent acts of grooming and pilgrimage are flexible in timing, reflecting the practical ease granted to pilgrims after fulfilling the obligatory duty.
